title: Reopen sends reversing entries dated the reopen date
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, with two stock parts picked from inventory: part A, quantity 2 at a cost of $40.00, and part B, quantity 1 at a cost of $25.00, whose Shop supplies amount was $15.00, closed with a posting date of the first day of this month.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete".

Step 6:

  • Reversing entries dated today with the memo "Reopened [number]" credit account X $80.00, $25.00 and $15.00 and debit the same accounts the Close credited.
  • After them account X carries $0.00 from this work order.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S7-R5: “At Reopen, ShopView sends reversing journal entries for exactly the entries it posted at Close, dated the reopen date, memo "Reopened [number]", as Reverse does for invoiced work orders today. Entries never posted (S7-N5, or still in QB Unexported) get no reversal (S4-E1).”
  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”
  • S10-R4: “At Close, the amount posts as one entry: debit the work order's expense account (the expense account of the work order's category), credit the shop supplies account (Story 7, S7-R4a; Story 8, S8-R3). Reopen reverses it (Story 4).”
